Deux flics de province tellement dépassés par leur enquête qu'ils préfèrent frapper des suspects au hasard et consulter une voyante plutôt que suivre une vraie méthode scientifique, l'académie de police coréenne n'a visiblement jamais entendu parler de la scène de crime qu'on ne piétine pas à dix personnes. Bong Joon-ho enchaîne les scènes qui devraient installer une tension glaçante mais qui basculent sans prévenir dans un comique presque slapstick, comme cette poursuite ridicule dans les champs de riz où l'un des flics dégringole une pente en pleine filature. La scène de l'interrogatoire musclé, censée être un tournant dramatique fort, se retrouve elle aussi parasitée par ce ton étrange qui hésite entre le grave et le grotesque. Et le twist final, où l'enquêteur revient des années plus tard sur les lieux sans jamais avoir eu de réponse claire, tombe complètement à plat après tant de tergiversations tonales. Bref, ce mélange volontaire d'humour et d'enquête criminelle ne m'a jamais permis de rentrer dans le film, ni par la peur ni par la tension, le tout m'ayant laissé complètement indifférent du début à la fin, 1 étoile.

Pissed me off. I get it, I understand why it ends the way it ends but it was so immensely frustrating it ruined the movie for me. And I get that that is the point!!! Admittedly, I didn’t know that this movie was based on a true story and that it was a cold case in 2003 until it ended and my brother told me, so know that I know that, I get it even more. And so I don’t necessarily dislike the idea of a no-answer (the final shot is amazing, yeah) — especially if that was the ‘truth’ at the time — and of course I get that the cops are meant to be corrupt and that the desperation of an unsolvable crime drives people to the brink, but I had a very hard time caring about men with power abusing it while women were being brutally murdered, seemingly in the background. I like Bong Joon Ho, and I didn’t think that this was a hyper misogynistic movie, but the brutality of the crimes felt so commonplace. The victims were consistently treated as a narrative afterthought and I just couldn’t bring myself to care about it at all. The cops torture men to get a confession for their own sake. Of course they don’t care about the women being raped and murdered with their own clothes, why would they? All they want is a confession, which is what the movie makes us care about. The women are an afterthought to the corruption. They are victims twice over, once in ‘practice’ (for lack of a better term), and for a second time when they are effectively forgotten about during the course of the investigation. And I get that that is sadly the way it almost always seems to be in real life, and perhaps the movie does it so well, it portrays that calloused, misogynistic corruption that seeps into everything so well that I couldn’t stand it. I felt like this meme while attempting to laugh at the dropkicks. How can I care about anything in the face of such brutality, especially when that brutality seems to be barely relevant? I don’t think it’s a bad movie, but I rarely write searching for objectivity, so I can only say that I hated it. Not for me at all. Once again, I understand why it does all that it does, and I guess I understand why it’s hailed as a Great, but I couldn’t look past how cavalier it was towards women being consistently brutalized. And I understand that perhaps that’s the way it’s meant to be, I guess it is a critique on that very calloused misogynistic corruption, but it feels a bit like the idea of an anti war movie. How can a movie not be misogynistic when most of its female characters are shown with their limbs splayed out on the ground? I’ve been very angry lately and I just can’t bring myself to ignore misogyny more than any woman does every day.

Let’s be honest: if you strip away all the pseudo-intellectual interpretations people have of this movie, it’s literally about nothing. It feels like everything that happens was made solely to build up to the ending. And yes, the ending is interesting in its own way, but it’s nowhere near as groundbreaking, revolutionary, or profound as people try to make it out to be. Movies like this existed before, were being made around the same time, and continued to be made afterward. There’s nothing particularly new here, other than the fact that this specific movie was made by Koreans. And if you take the ending away, there’s basically nothing left. The movie doesn’t stand out in any other way. There’s no particularly interesting detective element, no characters you actually want to follow, and no dialogue that’s especially engaging. Just exaggerated emotional reactions that start getting annoying after a while. It’s an incredibly boring movie. Yes, it has an idea, and yes, that idea is expressed reasonably well, but it’s hardly some extraordinary concept that magically makes up for everything else. It’s simply a mediocre movie about nothing that people seem to worship way too much — and, honestly, the only real reason I can see for that is that it was made in Korea. There just doesn’t seem to be any other explanation

Au vu de ses excellentes notes, le film n'est sûrement pas mauvais, mais c'est un style que je trouve inintéressant au possible. J'ai bien compris l'intention : utiliser l'enquête pour inverser la morale des deux inspecteurs et critiquer une police incompétente qui doit absolument fermer une enquête pour garder une réputation. L'idée est bonne, mais je me suis profondément ennuyé. L'enquête est omniprésente, mais manque cruellement de tension. On enchaîne les interrogatoires sans suspense avec des suspects ridicules, comme le mec en slip à plumes roses suspendu au plafond ou le personnage autiste utilisé comme ressort comique. Cette ambiance tout sauf sérieuse, avec des flics qui lâchent des high kick sortis de nulle part, m'a totalement sorti de l'atmosphère sombre et mystérieuse que j'attends d'un thriller. Du coup, quand la fameuse évolution psychologique des personnages finit par arriver, il est trop tard, l'ennui m'avait déjà fait décrocher. C'est dommage : si le film avait associé ce développement intelligent à une vraie ambiance oppressante et des suspects intrigants, il m'aurait marqué. En l'état, il est complètement passé à côté de mes attentes.

It tries to discuss an issue and send a strong message while also not taking the subject matter seriously . It is unnecessarily misogynistic while tackling a series of crimes that are sexist and gender based in nature . It shows a detective unnecessarily beating a woman in one scene, and in another scene a detective tries to beat a woman for “sleeping with a professor”, and in yet another scene a detective talks about how “beautiful” the rape and femicide victims are, as if gender based sexual crimes and violence were ever about how beautiful or sexy you are . So many unnecessary dialogues and scenes of women being degraded and sexist harmful rhetoric being spewed as if it is nothing and just like any other dialogue . I can tell the director is a misogynistic woman hating freak based off how lightly the movie handles its subject . The male characters objectify and abuse women “humorously” throughout the film . Tratto da eventi storici realmente accaduti, ovvero gli omicidi seriali avvenuti a Hwaseong in una provincia rurale della Corea del Sud. "Memories of Murder" è stato uno dei maggior successi commerciali dell'apprezzato regista coreano Bong Joon-ho. Anche se l'incipit della narrazione e il modus operandi del serial killer vengono descritti in modo del tutto ordinario. Memories of Murder si discosta dal solito poliziesco per quel ricordo, un frammento di eventi autoctoni svaniti nel tempo che tornano alla mente solo nel finale, capace di trasportare lo spettatore occidentale in un mondo parzialmente estraneo. L'opera di Bong Joo-ho è dunque degna di interesse perchè porta alla superficie una concreta denuncia sociale, una pertinente e aspra critica alla società, nello specifico quella delle forze di Polizia, fondata sul concetto autartico dell'ego. Un ego smisurato che non si preoccupa minimamente del concetto di variabilità dell'ipotesi. Ciò che conta di più è portare a termine le indagini ad ogni costo, e insabbiare alla stampa certe pratiche ortodosse adottate a discapito dei sospettati. Tipiche pratiche fra l'altro molto diffuse nella cultura asiatica.. Il film cattura l'interesse già da subito grazie all'ottimo cast, Sang Kang-ho (Parasite), Park Ha-il, Kim Roi-ha, Kim Sang-Kyung, Jung In-sun etc, e all'ambientazione rurale piovosa e a una fotografia degna di nota. Aimé non mancano delle forzature per "incanalare" la sceneggiatura negli eventi voluti, e l'importante minutaggio evidenzia dei dettagli di trama superflui. Ma la soggettiva peculiarità della trama sta tutta racchiusa nel finale amaro quanto drammaticamente evocativo. La curiosità, e il rammarico di aver sbagliato scuotono i sensi del protagonista e dello spettatore.. Dove il cinismo del passato riemerge e si impadronisce di nuovo della ragione, ma quello che ne rimane e soltanto l'immaginazione di un volto comune. Troppo comune.. Visione consigliatissima. Voto: più che sufficiente.

An interesting movie. Being a satire of detective thrillers, the movie exaggerates the violence and incompetence of the main policemen. Being a crime thriller, it follows the investigation of a serial murderer and rapist. These two ideas do not mesh. The vast majority of the movie is dead serious, and there is one character who drop kicks every suspect they interrogate. The only overtly satirical element (that I caught) really throws the tone of the movie out of whack for me. However, the movie always treats the crimes themselves (based on true events) with respect, thankfully. The only characters that we are not to truly take seriously are the idiot cops. The first hour and a half felt very repetitive, as they find another suspect, beat them up and threaten them, then move on once they realize it’s the wrong person. Perhaps another joke on the behalf of the police, but it doesn’t make it fun to watch— it was frustrating at best, annoying at worst. The last 30 minutes or so really drew me in, and especially the last two scenes. The cinematography throughout the whole movie was quite good, but was racheted up as the movie moved from desaturated, darkly lit scenes to brighter, higher exposure scenes. The train tunnel’s blackness and the fields yellow contrasting the bright sky made the final two scenes a joy to watch. If the rest of the movie was just as artful in craft, and emotional in content, I would’ve really loved the film.

When first watching Memories of Murder: I had heard that it was a masterpiece of True Crime filmmaking. I had watched many Korean horror films but this was the first drama/true crime foreign film. I'll admit, I didn't really get it the first time. All the detectives are kind of inept and do some pretty bad things themselves. So who do we route for? And that ending .... What!? But for years it stuck with me. So I started looking into it and realized "Oh, this was based on an actual serial killing in South Korea." And not just a serial killing, but what many would consider to be the first modern serial killer in South Korea. The director, Bong Joon-ho, probably remembered and experienced some of this growing up.  The police were actually pretty inept did infact torture confessions from people and were in over their heads. While creative liberties were taken, timelines shortened and some people involved changes: the telling is quite accurate. Knowing that now, Memories of Murder becomes much more engaging, interesting and poignant. All of our characters are shades of grey because the detectives were in fact torturing confessions from people, were incredibly under resources and frequently went off of feelings or hunches because of a lack of evidence. While being culturallydifferent from traditional American detective stories (Zodiac and Seven come to mind) once you get used to the Korean style and culture, with some added understanding of the true events that inspire the story, Memories of Murder really is a master piece in true crime filmmaking. It is also an interesting look at a director's early work that would carry them into greater future success.

Gerade geguckt: „Memories of Murder“ ist ein Kriminal Thriller welcher 1986, in einer kleinen Provinz, im von der Militärdiktatur geprägten Südkorea spielt. Es geht um zwei ungleiche Kommissarre, die versuchen eine Reihe von Morden aufzuklären, welche immer an einem verregneten Tag und an rot gekleideten Frauen begangen werden. Allerdings ist der Film nicht nur ein einfacher Krimi sondern auch eine Nachricht an den echten Mörder, welcher erst 16 Jahre nach dem erscheinen des Films gefasst wurde. Abgesehen davon Thematisiert der Film die Inkompetenz der Polizei und den moralischen Verfall einer der Kommissare sowie Südkorea im Chaos des kurz bevorstehenden Umbruchs der Diktatur. Regisseur Bong Joon-ho zeichnet mit „Memorie of Murder“ ein atmosphärisches und immer düsterer werdendes Portrait einer traumatisierten Gesellschaft in wunderschönen aber dreckigen Bildern. Die letzte Szene ging mit einem einfachen aber tief gehenden Blick in die Kamera, nicht zu Unrecht in die Filmgeschichte ein. „Memories of Murder“ wird mir wahrscheinlich noch die nächsten Tage im Gedächtnis bleiben und motiviert mich weiter in Bong Joon-ho‘s Vita und das Koreanische Kino einzutauchen. Meiner Meinung nach einer der besten Filme seines Genres, die ich bis jetzt gesehen habe. Kann ich jedem empfehlen. (Btw noch nie so viele Dropkicks in einem ernsten Film gesehen)
